correctness.rationale: For the precise standard Padovan initialization (1,1,1), the matrix T has order 48 on the vector modulo seven and \(T^{48}=I+7B\) with (T^48-I)v/7 nonzero modulo seven. Thus the least periods are \(48\cdot7^{k-1}\). Exact coefficient tables show nine simple branches and three singular branches whose divided-by-49 reductions have two simple roots apiece. Hensel lifting gives respectively one and fourteen indices in each prime-power period for k>=3, so counts 12, 30, 51 are proved rather than extrapolated. The limiting valuation probabilities follow by subtracting periodic divisibility densities. check.py independently recomputes the finite data and six whole periods. Residual risk is confined to errors in the written analytic lifting reasoning, not the finite arithmetic; that reasoning was checked separately.

value.rationale: The count of zero values modulo prime powers is a natural invariant of a recurrence, not a hand-picked numerical target. Its stabilization at 51 despite period growth is structurally explained by a nontrivial split into nine regular branches and three doubly lifting singular branches. This yields exact densities for every 7-adic valuation, a complete local distribution beyond the period and isolated modular congruence facts in the related literature. The prime-specific scope and lack of full nonzero-residue census are explicit limitations, but the infinite classification is mathematically motivated and non-routine.
